## All 3 ACs met against a fresh run — closing

The fix landed on `origin/main` as **`0bce6a724255c4ece2add93c65e174f3d0926d1d`** ("Pull
MinIO from quay.io instead of Docker Hub"), trailer `rebar-ticket: 6d98-28f4-946a-4016`.

### AC1 — valid, pullable MinIO reference: MET

The compose file now pulls from **quay.io** with a **pinned** release tag
(`RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`) instead of the vanished `minio/minio:latest`. The commit
message records the diagnosis properly: the Docker Hub API returned 404 for the repository
and a token-authed manifest request returned 401, so the image was genuinely gone rather
than misauthenticated — no credential would have made the old reference pullable.

Pinning rather than tracking `latest` is the better half of that fix. `latest` was the only
floating tag in the file (langfuse, clickhouse, redis and postgres were already pinned), so
a scheduled run could previously change this image underneath itself with no commit. That
is the class of failure, not just the instance.

### AC2 — fresh run no longer fails in the langfuse job: MET

Run **35508005436** on `main`, 2026-09-20T11:30Z. Per-job conclusions:

```
success    langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)   <-- this ticket
success    external LLM (live bedrock / openai / anthropic)
success    external integration (live services)
success    jira Cloud coordinator mutation probe
success    Pandoc corpus replay (ubuntu-latest / macos-latest)
skipped    jira Cloud + S3 rehearsal
failure    jira DC harness smoke (real Jira Data Center, ephemeral)
```

The langfuse job reaches its assertions and passes. No `pull access denied` anywhere in the
run.

### AC3 — the Jira DC harness failure is tracked separately, with readable logs: MET

It still fails, it is tracked separately, and — unlike the 404 that scoped this ticket in
the first place — its logs are now readable. The failure is disk exhaustion, not anything
Langfuse-related:

```
13:41:05Z ##[warning] You are running out of disk space ... Free space left: 23 MB
13:41:45Z fatal: sha1 file '.../dc-multi-store-copy/.tickets-tracker/.git/index.lock'
          write error. Out of diskspace
13:41:45Z ##[error] No space left on device
          CalledProcessError: ['git','commit','-q','--no-verify','-m',
          'scrubbed store copy for 368f DC rehearsal'] returned non-zero exit status 128
```

That is exactly **`25e0-4d88-83d9-4253`** (the harness copies the whole ticket store per
test and exhausts the runner disk) — change **3012** is in review for it.

The same job also went **11:35 → 13:41, two hours and six minutes, with no output** before
failing, which is exactly **`2277-7043`** — change **3008** is in review for that.

So the lane's remaining red is fully attributed to two separate tickets that each have a
change in flight, and nothing is left unowned under this ticket.

### Scope note

This ticket was scoped to the Langfuse failure deliberately, because the Jira DC job's logs
404'd at filing time. That scoping held up: the Langfuse cause was independent, is fixed,
and the DC job's cause turned out to be a different defect entirely.
